the role of wind in controlling the accumulation of heavy metal in sediment of Lake Uluabat.
the role of wind in the accumulation of heavy metal in the sediments of a shallow, freshwater lake in Turkey.
the sedimentation processes in a large lake, the accumulation of heavy elements in lake sediment, the effect of wind, and the role of the lake in the transport of sediments and heavy elements.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the heavy metals were deposited in Lake Ulubat, but the sedimentary record is not preserved due to the high wind energy in the region.
the lake sediments are silt-dominated and have a low heavy-metal content due to wind-induced resuspension and transport of the fine particles and heavy metals.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the wind-controlled sediment accumulation in the lake is responsible for its heavy metal-depleted character.
the lake sediments are not a reliable archive for the heavy metal history.
wind is the most important factor in the sedimentation of Lake Ulubat and the accumulation of heavy metal.
The main takeaway from our work is that
shallow lakes are not good sinks for heavy metals.
the accumulation of heavy metal concentrations in the sediments of Lake Ulubat are controlled by the wind.
the sedimentary records in Lake Ulubat are not suitable for reconstructing environmental changes, especially heavy metal contamination, in the drainage basin.
